messages.subject: Arrival-Specific Signals
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

If two arrivals are waiting for the same signal to be sent, how can I release only 1 of them when the signal is sent rather than both of them?

Best,
John

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Arrival-Specific Signals
messages.body_plain:
El lun., 17 sept. 2018 a las 15:46, John Redmond
(<john.re...@gmail.com>) escribió:

>
> Hi,
>
> If two arrivals are waiting for the same signal to be sent, how can I release only 1 of them when the signal is sent rather than both of them?

If it's the same signal, you can't. However, you can set up a
single-capacity resource and then use seize's "reject" trajectory to
make all the arrivals but one to rollback to the "wait" activity
again. Or you can directly use resources instead of signals.

Iñaki

>
> Best,
> John
>

El lun., 17 sept. 2018 a las 16:49, John Redmond
(<john.re...@gmail.com>) escribió:
>

> Okay - that may work for my purpose. If not, is there a way to build a custom function I can insert into the trajectory which appends to a global array?
>
> Something like this:
>
>   bailer_wait_push <<- function(.trj, g_id) {
>     .trj %>% timeout(0)
>
>     bailer_wait_queue <<- append(bailer_wait_queue,g_id)
>
>   }

What do you want to append? get_name() retrieves the arrival name,
which is a unique identifier. You may want to use that as the signal
name.

trap(function() {
  sig <- get_name(env)
  some_vec <<- c(some_vec, sig)
  sig
}) %>%
wait()

and then

send(function() {
  sig <- some_vec[1]
  some_vec <<- some_vec[-1]
  sig
})

Iñaki
